title: Two Lives, One Patch? Lichens Explained Simply | PUC Biology Class 11
description:
Aarav rides past grey-green patches on the rocks of his bicycle road every day, yet the walls of a smoky city have none. Diya tells him the patch is not one living thing, but two. This lesson shows who the two partners are, what each one gives, and why lichens vanish from dirty air.

A live zoom ladder goes from the rock to one lichen, a thin slice with its packed hyphae and green algal layer, and one algal cell wrapped in fungal hyphae. The trade runs step by step: the phycobiont (alga, autotrophic) makes food, the mycobiont (fungus, heterotrophic) gives shelter, water and minerals. Then lichens as pollution indicators, mutualism vs commensalism vs parasitism side by side (lichen, mycorrhiza, an orchid on a mango branch, Albugo, the cattle egret), a worked sort of five partnerships, the exam trap on who makes the food, an original NEET assertion-reason question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

This is Episode 17 of our PUC Biology series.
Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11 and NEET students.
